edges.description: Why complex I failure selects retinal ganglion cells is the central unsolved question of the inherited optic neuropathies generally, and no NDUFAF8-specific work addresses it. The edge is typed as having unknown intermediates for that reason.

edges.description: The route from a generalised bioenergetic deficit to the specific symmetrical brainstem and basal-ganglia lesions of Leigh syndrome is not established for NDUFAF8 or for complex I deficiency as a class.
Supplying wild-type NDUFAF8 corrected both the assembly defect and the biochemical deficiency in the patients' own cells, which excludes a coincidental variant and localises the deficit to this gene.
edges.limitations: Fibroblasts are neither brain nor retinal ganglion cell, and neither affected tissue has been studied. The rescue establishes causality; it says nothing about why the basal ganglia or the optic nerve are the organs that fail, nor about why the same gene produces two such different clinical pictures.

nodes.description:
The initiating lesion. Two allele classes have been reported and they are instructive in different ways.
The first is a deep-intronic splicing variant, c.195+271C>T, which the defining study found recurrently and which it explicitly flags as having been initially overlooked because of where it sits. That is a diagnostic warning with a general moral, drawn by the authors themselves: when a patient has one definitively pathogenic variant in a recessive gene and no second hit, the intronic sequence is where to look. The same allele is what links the Leigh and optic-atrophy cohorts.
The second is c.44T>G p.(L15R), which lies in the mitochondrial targeting sequence rather than in a functional domain, and is predicted to introduce a positive charge on the hydrophobic face of the amphipathic targeting helix. The consequence proposed for it is a failure of import rather than a failure of function, which is a different kind of loss-of-function claim and is modelled as its own node below.

Both are recorded in the `inheritance:` block instead.

nodes.description:
The only treatment with any published relationship to this disease, and it is a recommendation rather than a result.
The 2026 series that found the optic-atrophy pole of NDUFAF8 disease concludes that patients with nuclear complex I optic neuropathy may benefit from idebenone, dosed as it is for Leber hereditary optic neuropathy - where it is an approved therapy. The same paper reports what its cohort actually experienced, and the honest reading is discouraging: visual improvement was variable, with only three of thirteen patients showing some degree of response.
Three limits on how far this should be taken. The three-of-thirteen figure sits in a paragraph describing the whole thirty-one-patient series, directly after the sentence listing which drugs were used, so the thirteen are most plausibly the patients who received idebenone - the cache does not say. What it is emphatically not is thirteen NDUFAF8 patients, and it should not be read as the paper's thirteen assembly-factor patients either, even though that group happens to number thirteen too: taking the coincidence for a match would imply six of the treated thirteen carry NDUFAF8, a far tighter link than anything the paper states. No response rate can be attributed to this genotype from it. No NDUFAF8 patient's individual treatment or outcome is reported anywhere. And nothing has been reported at all for the Leigh-syndrome pole, where an optic-nerve-directed therapy would not address the encephalopathy. This block records a recommendation the literature makes for a class this disease belongs to; it is not evidence that idebenone helps MC1DN34.

nodes.description:
The measured biochemical endpoint, and the phenotype the disease is named for. Patient fibroblasts express a complex I deficiency; the deficiency is isolated, meaning the other respiratory-chain complexes are spared, which is what an assembly factor dedicated to complex I predicts and what distinguishes this from the combined deficiencies caused by defects in mitochondrial gene expression. Lentiviral transduction with wild-type NDUFAF8 cDNA corrected both the assembly defect and the biochemical deficiency, which is the experiment that makes the gene causal rather than merely associated.
Conformance note: the module node pairs decreased oxidative phosphorylation with increased reactive oxygen species. Only the first half is evidenced here - no reactive-oxygen measurement has been reported in an NDUFAF8 patient - and the ROS arm is not asserted. The module's upstream node, age-related mitochondrial damage and mtDNA mutation, does not apply to a primary nuclear-gene assembly defect, so conformance is declared at this node alone.

nodes.description:
The 2020 pole of the phenotype. All three subjects in the defining cohort carried a clinical diagnosis of Leigh syndrome - the commonest neurological presentation of paediatric mitochondrial disease, defined by symmetrical basal-ganglia, thalamic and brainstem lesions on neuroimaging together with loss of motor skills and delayed milestones.
A scope note that matters for how this node should be read. The subjects' Leigh diagnosis is directly stated in the source; the lesion distribution and developmental features are quoted from the source's definition of Leigh syndrome rather than from a description of these three children. The diagnosis entails those features, which is why they are recorded here, but no per-patient imaging or developmental description is available in the cached record. The `phenotypes:` block reflects that distinction: it curates the Leigh diagnosis, not a list of individually observed neurological signs.

nodes.description:
NDUFAF8 does not act alone, and this is the node that explains why an assembly-factor loss is not simply a slower assembly. NDUFAF8 was found in the first place as an interactor of NDUFAF5, and the dependency runs the other way too: NDUFAF5 requires NDUFAF8 for its stability, so NDUFAF8 loss removes both halves of the module. Together the two contribute to the early stabilisation of NDUFS7, a core subunit of the matrix Q module.
The measured consequence in a patient is a NDUFAF5 level at 18 percent of control. That is the strongest quantitative statement available anywhere in this entity, and it is a measurement of the partner rather than of NDUFAF8.
The GO binding here is deliberately not the complex I assembly term its neighbouring nodes carry. What this node asserts is narrower and prior to assembly: NDUFAF8 holding NDUFAF5 stable, measured as an 82 percent fall in NDUFAF5 when NDUFAF8 is lost. Protein stabilization is what that is, and using it keeps the three nodes in this stretch of the chain distinguishable rather than tagging all of them with the same process.

nodes.description: Fibroblasts from the three Leigh-syndrome subjects, transduced with wild-type NDUFAF8 cDNA. This is the experiment that converted a candidate gene into a disease gene, and it is the only functional work reported in cells from a patient with this disorder. There is no NDUFAF8 animal model, no knockout cell line reported in a disease context, and no patient tissue.

Present in six patients from three families in the 2026 cohort, isolated in five of them, with subacute onset in a proportion of the assembly-factor patients - a Leber-like rather than an insidious dominant-optic-atrophy picture.
It is not confined to that cohort. As an uncited lead from the deep-research report committed with this entry: the 2020 Leigh cohort's subject 1 had optic atrophy and visual impairment, and its subject 2 had small optic nerves and nystagmus. The evidence item below cites only the 2026 cohort because that is what is snippet-verifiable, but the phenotype should not be read as belonging to the mild pole alone.

nodes.description:
Whatever the allele class, the shared consequence is that less functional NDUFAF8 reaches the mitochondrial matrix. For the deep-intronic allele the route is transcript decay. For p.(L15R) the proposed route is import failure: the residue lies in the targeting sequence, and the 2026 study reports experimental support that the variant reduces NDUFAF8 abundance in mitochondria and impairs complex I assembly.
The evidence for the abundance claim in that family is indirect and the entry should be read as saying so. Quantitative proteomics on the patient's fibroblasts did not detect NDUFAF8 at all in the batch, so the protein's own level was not measured; what was measured was a strong fall in NDUFAF5, which is the protein whose stability depends on NDUFAF8, and a moderate fall in complex I. That is a coherent read-out of NDUFAF8 loss through its obligate partner, and it is how the node is supported, but it is not a direct measurement of NDUFAF8.

nodes.description:
The 2026 pole of the phenotype. Six patients with biallelic NDUFAF8 variants presented with optic atrophy, five of them with optic atrophy and nothing else; the sixth also had cerebellar ataxia and nystagmus. In six of the thirteen patients across the four assembly-factor genes in that cohort the vision loss was subacute, which is the pattern of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy, and NDUFAF8 was associated with the autosomal-recessive LHON phenotype for the first time.
Marked PROVISIONAL rather than ESTABLISHED because the *cellular* claim in the node title is an inference. What was observed is optic atrophy in patients; retinal ganglion cell loss is the accepted substrate of optic atrophy in the mitochondrial optic neuropathies but was not measured in these patients, and no NDUFAF8 tissue has been examined.

nodes.description:
Complex I is built stepwise from modular intermediates, and where a defect stalls that process is visible directly by complexome profiling. In NDUFAF8 patient fibroblasts the profile shows an assembly defect whose stalled intermediates place NDUFAF8's role early - consistent with the module's substrate being a core Q-module subunit rather than a late accessory addition.
This is the node that separates MC1DN34 from a subunit deficiency. A missing subunit yields an enzyme that is assembled but incomplete or inactive; a missing early assembly factor yields an enzyme that never gets past an intermediate.
